key_insight: Bayesian Dialectical Argumentation turns multi-LLM discussion traces into reliability estimates, so the council can produce calibrated probabilities and resist persistent bad actors.
engineering_relevance: For deployed LLM councils, BDA offers a zero-extra-call way to improve trustworthiness, making confidence scores closer to true correctness likelihood while remaining robust to unreliable participants.
method: Model typed council moves (propose/challenge/concede) as observations in a Bayesian annotator framework.
Infer per-agent reliability from the deliberation trace, including the possibility of adversarial or inverted agents.
Aggregate answers by weighting evidence with inferred reliability to output calibrated posteriors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on binary and multi-class benchmarks, where BDA achieved the best calibration among zero-cost council aggregation methods and improved robustness under persistent adversarial coalitions.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and consistency of typed deliberation traces, so councils that do not log clear move types may be harder to model reliably.
paper_title: Counting Moves, Weighing Voices: Bayesian Dialectical Argumentation for Calibrated Multi-LLM Councils under Persistent Adversaries
